status_detail: The prototype builds, signs, validates, and the XCTest passes with Xcode beta. LaunchServices still refuses to open the generated app bundle with kLSNoExecutableErr. A minimal generated /private/tmp app bundle with a C executable also fails with the same LaunchServices error while running directly, so the remaining launch blocker is classified as LaunchServices/session handling of generated bundles, not the prototype executable or Info.plist alone.
dirty_state_before: Branch codex/improve-native-release-ratchets was behind origin by 1 with unrelated qwen/release-ratchet/prototype dirty files already present. This lane preserved unrelated dirty work.
dirty_state_after: Prototype-local launcher and startup receipt instrumentation changed. Unrelated qwen/PR/release-ratchet dirt remains preserved.

artifact_assertions.assertion: The launcher now builds with SwiftPM, writes PkgInfo, signs the bundle, and writes deterministic build/launch receipts.
The app writes a startup receipt when IMPROVE_AGENT_NATIVE_STARTUP_RECEIPT is set.
Direct executable startup wrote status=started and process_identifier=75408.
LaunchServices launch receipt records status=failed and startup receipt remains missing.

termination_method_evidence: Launch.command attempts application-scoped quit through osascript for bundle id local.jscraik.improve-agent-native-menubar.
Launch.command attempts application-scoped quit through osascript for application name Improve Agent Native.
Launch.command attempts pkill -x ImproveAgentNativeMenuBar and pkill -f the exact app executable path.
No killed PIDs can be reported because process enumeration is blocked by the sandbox.
what_proves: The generated bundle has correct executable/plist/signature shape.
The launcher now builds and packages the latest SwiftPM executable.
The app binary can start far enough to emit its startup receipt on direct execution.
LaunchServices failure reproduces on a minimal generated app, so the remaining blocker is not unique to this prototype bundle.
what_remains_unproven: Menu bar UI is visible through LaunchServices.
LaunchServices can open generated local app bundles in this Codex session.
Hosted PR state, SDK release readiness, oss-cloud, Tessl dry-run, or Tessl live behavior.
owner_classification: LaunchServices/session handling of generated local app bundles; prototype executable, Info.plist, signing, and xattrs have evidence against being the sole owner.

contradictions.problem: LaunchServices reports kLSNoExecutableErr even when the executable exists, plist points to it, architecture is arm64, and codesign verifies. The same failure occurs for a minimal generated probe app.

lessons.lesson: LaunchServices proof must be separated from app-binary startup proof.
lessons.failure_pattern: A valid generated app bundle and a minimal probe both fail under LaunchServices while the direct binary can emit startup proof.
lessons.deterministic_guardrail: Require build receipt, launch receipt, and app-emitted startup receipt as separate artifacts; classify LaunchServices failures separately from packaging failures after a minimal probe reproduces them.

remaining_blockers.detail: open returns kLSNoExecutableErr for both the prototype bundle and a minimal generated signed app bundle, even though both executables exist and run directly.
The checkout contains unrelated qwen/release-ratchet dirty files and branch is behind origin by 1, so no commit was attempted from this mixed worktree.

next_action: Validate the app bundle from Finder or a normal Terminal session outside this Codex sandbox, or add a controlled installed-app staging path if LaunchServices only accepts bundles from trusted user app locations in this environment.
recommended_next_pm_decision: Treat build/test as passing but launch as blocked by LaunchServices/session behavior. Decide whether to test outside Codex sandbox or add an installed-app staging lane before more prototype source edits.
